1.value: 📖  GLOSSARY  —  Technical terminology, definitions, and source citations

Every technical term used in this toolkit with its plain-English definition and authoritative source. Cell comments throughout the workbook point back to this glossary. Where a term has both an international standard reference and a South African legal reference, both are cited.

3.value: Definition
Atmospheric gases that trap heat: CO₂, CH₄ (methane), N₂O (nitrous oxide), HFCs, PFCs, SF₆, NF₃.
Common unit for GHGs. Converts each gas to equivalent warming impact of CO₂ over 100 years using GWP factors.
Multiplier converting non-CO₂ gases to CO₂e. CH₄ = 27.9, N₂O = 273, SF₆ = 25,200.
Direct emissions from owned/controlled sources. Fleet fuel, generators, on-site combustion, refrigerant leaks.
Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, steam, heating, cooling.
All other indirect emissions across the value chain (15 categories incl. purchased goods, business travel, employee commute, waste, water, downstream transport).

4.value: GHG Protocol Corp. Value Chain Standard

3.value: Coefficient converting activity data (litres, kWh, kg) into emissions (kgCO₂e). e.g. diesel = 2.68 kgCO₂e/L.
World Resources Institute/WBCSD standard for corporate GHG accounting. The foundational reference for Scope 1/2/3 classification.
Voluntary framework defining "credible" emissions reduction targets aligned to limiting warming to 1.5°C / well-below 2°C.
SBTi standard requiring ≥90% emissions reduction across all scopes by long-term target year, with residuals neutralised via permanent removals.
Global initiative committing members to 100% renewable electricity.
South African Carbon Tax Act 15 of 2019, Section 12L. Levy on Scope 1+2 emissions above the basic 60% tax-free allowance. Tier 1 rate R236/tCO₂e (2025); escalating.
Income Tax Act §12L. 60% basic tax-free emissions allowance for industrial/commercial firms. Reduces taxable Scope 1+2 base.

4.value: Income Tax Act s12L; SARS guidance

3.value: International standard for quantifying GHG emissions from transport chains. Defines journey-level calculation, allocation methods, and intensity metrics.
Global Logistics Emissions Council framework. The practical methodology that operationalises ISO 14083 for industry. Maintained by Smart Freight Centre.
Activity unit for transport emissions: 1 tonne of cargo moved 1 km. Calculated as Load (t) × Distance (km).
Grams of CO₂e per tonne-kilometre. Standard transport KPI. Benchmark for heavy road freight: 80 g/t·km (GLEC).
ISO 14083 preferred method. Calculate emissions from actual fuel consumed × emission factor. Highest data quality.
Fallback when fuel data unavailable. Multiplies distance × vehicle-class default emission factor.
Splitting trip emissions across multiple customers/shipments. Bases: weight, volume, distance, revenue, equal-share.
Unloaded return leg. Emissions of an empty trip are typically allocated to the loaded trip(s).
Three-pillar framework for non-financial corporate performance disclosure.
IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard 1: General requirements for sustainability-related financial disclosures.
IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard 2: Climate-related disclosures. Incorporates TCFD recommendations.
Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures. Four-pillar climate disclosure framework: Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets. Subsumed by IFRS S2 from 2024.
Global Reporting Initiative — most widely used voluntary sustainability disclosure standard. Universal (GRI 1-3) + Topic (200/300/400 series).
European Sustainability Reporting Standards. Mandatory under EU CSRD. Stricter than IFRS — requires double materiality.
Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (EU). Phased mandate from 2024. Requires ESRS-compliant reporting + assurance.
Financial materiality only — what impacts the company. IFRS approach.
Financial materiality + impact materiality (how company impacts environment/society). ESRS approach.
Information is material if its omission/misstatement would influence stakeholder decisions. Quantified via materiality matrix.
Plot of issues by impact (x-axis) vs likelihood/stakeholder interest (y-axis). Highlights priority topics.
South African corporate governance code. 17 principles applying "Apply & Explain" methodology. Mandatory for JSE-listed firms.
King V methodology: governing body either confirms application of a principle (and explains how) or explains non-application.
Companies Act §1 calculation determining audit/S&EC requirements. Based on turnover, employee count, beneficial holders, third-party liabilities. ≥500 = mandatory S&EC + independent audit.
Mandatory committee for companies with PI score ≥500 or listed. Monitors EE, B-BBEE, anti-corruption, consumer relations, CSI, environment.
Risk Governance — board oversight of opportunities and risks (incl. ESG/climate).
Disclosure — transparent reporting on the organisation's performance and prospects.
Coordinated assurance from management, internal audit, external audit, and specialists across the same risk areas.
South African legislation driving economic transformation. Generic Scorecard has 5 elements + bonus = 114 points.
Default B-BBEE scorecard applicable to firms not under a sector charter. 5 elements: Ownership, MC, SD, ESD, SED.
B-BBEE Element 1 (25 pts). % Black ownership in entity. Statement 100.
B-BBEE Element 2 (19 pts). Black representation at board/senior management. Statement 200.
B-BBEE Element 3 (25 pts). 6% payroll spend on Black training. Statement 300.
B-BBEE Element 4 (40 pts). Preferential procurement + supplier dev contributions. Statement 400.
B-BBEE Element 5 (5 pts). 1% NPAT spend on CSI for Black beneficiaries. Statement 500.
Ownership calculation method. Where a Black-owned entity holds ≥51% of a measured entity, treat that holding as 100% Black for one level only.
Default ownership calculation — multiply Black % through each level of holding company structure.
Annual turnover ≤R10m. Auto-Level 4 (Generic) or Level 2 (≥51% Black-owned). Affidavit-based.
Annual turnover R10m–R50m. Simplified scorecard with 4 elements.
Sworn statement confirming EME/QSE status. Replaces verified certificate for EMEs.
B-BBEE points awarded for buying from Level 1-8 suppliers. 25 of the 40 ESD points.
South African legislation requiring designated employers to eliminate unfair discrimination and implement affirmative action.
Annual employment equity report submitted to Department of Employment & Labour (DoEL). Breaks down workforce by race, gender, disability across 6 occupational levels.
Standard SA occupational level classification: L1 Top Mgmt, L2 Senior Mgmt, L3 Professionally Qualified, L4 Skilled Technical, L5 Semi-Skilled, L6 Unskilled.
EEA-recognised disabled persons. Target: ≥2% of workforce.

4.value: EEA s6 + Code of Good Practice on PWD

3.value: Annual training plan submitted to SETA by 30 April. Sets out training to be delivered.
Annual report on training actually delivered. Submitted with WSP by 30 April.
Industry-specific authority for skills development. TETA (Transport), WRSETA (Wholesale & Retail), etc.
1% of payroll levy paid to SARS, distributed to SETAs. WSP/ATR submission unlocks mandatory grant recovery (20% of levy).
Organising Framework for Occupations. National occupation classification used in WSP/ATR submissions. e.g. 911101 = Heavy Motor Vehicle Drivers.
20% of SDL levy returned to employer for compliant WSP/ATR submission.
Up to 49.5% of SDL levy available for SETA-approved training projects (learnerships, bursaries).
South African statute setting workplace H&S obligations.
Number of lost-time injuries per 1,000,000 hours worked. Target ≤2.0. = (LTIs × 1,000,000) / hours worked.
Number of LTI + MTI (medical-treatment injuries) per 1,000,000 hours worked. Target ≤4.0.
Workplace injury resulting in ≥1 shift of lost work.
Workplace injury requiring more than first-aid treatment but not lost time.
International standard for occupational H&S management systems. Replaced OHSAS 18001 in 2018.
International standard for environmental management systems. Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle with aspects register, legal compliance, continuous improvement.
Element of an organisation's activities that interacts with the environment (e.g. fleet diesel combustion = air emissions aspect).
National Environmental Management Act — SA framework act for environmental governance. Section 28 = duty of care.
National Environmental Management: Waste Act. Defines waste hierarchy, licensing for waste activities.
SA legislation governing water use. Section 21 = water use licensing.
% of total waste diverted from landfill via recycling, recovery, reuse. Target ≥75% (ISO 14001 / NEMWA hierarchy).
Protection of Personal Information Act. SA equivalent of GDPR. Effective from July 2021.
POPIA-mandated role accountable for compliance. Must be registered with Information Regulator.
International standard for information security management systems. ISMS controls aligned to Annex A.
International guidance standard for social responsibility. Not certifiable. 7 core subjects.
Global Association of Risk Professionals. Source of widely-adopted ERM framework for financial and operational risk.
Generally Recognised Accounting Practices. Public sector accounting framework in SA. Used here for "public interest" risk alignment.
Integrated framework for identifying, assessing, treating, and monitoring risks across the enterprise.
International standard for risk management principles and guidelines.
After-tax profit attributable to shareholders. Base for SED 1% target.
Corporate Social Investment / Socio-Economic Development spend. B-BBEE SED target = 1% NPAT.
International Standard on Assurance Engagements for non-financial assurance (sustainability reports, ESG disclosures).
Johannesburg Stock Exchange rulebook. Section 8.63 = ESG/sustainability reporting; King V mandatory.
